headline: Dutch Lawmakers Back Controversial Bill, Threatening Coalition
content: (Bloomberg) -- Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten made a last-minute bid to keep his government from collapsing as lawmakers backed a controversial wealth tax amendment that could sink his coalition. Jetten’s center-left D66 and another party in his three-way coalition made a deal with left-wing opposition groups to pass legislation to shift the country’s tax burden from income to wealth-related measures — lawmakers narrowly approved the amendment Thursday. The People’s Party, the third group in the governing coalition, previously threatened to quit if the measure passed. It wasn’t clear after the vote what the People’s Party’s next steps would be. A spokesperson from the group didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. “The past few weeks have certainly had an impact on the relationships and trust within the coalition and the cabinet,” Jetten said in parliament on Thursday. “I also see that there are three coalition parties that formed a cabinet at the beginning of this year out of the conviction that we need to work together to break the deadlock on a few stalled issues.”The AEX index, a key indicator of the Dutch stock market, was little changed Thursday, closing down 0.4%. The disagreement reflects the power wielded by several political parties in the fragmented Dutch parliament, where bartering over a wide range of issues for each particular vote has led to deadlock. Jetten’s government doesn’t have a majority in either house of parliament, and as a result has to rely on support from left- and right-wing parties to pass legislation. If the People’s Party were to leave the coalition it would potentially bring down Jetten’s nine-month-old government. The controversial element of the amendment has been dubbed the millionaires’ tax. It proposes taxing returns on assets above €60,000 ($66,555) per year at 38.5%, among the highest rates in the euro region. The rate below the threshold would drop to 35.5%. That rate is 36% currently, regardless of the amount.The new rules would also crack down on efforts to avoid inheritance taxes through so-called paper gifts, when money is legally given but not transferred.According to projections from the parties supporting the amendment, the budgetary impact of the proposal would shift about €1 billion of tax burden from income to wealth. But some criticized the government crisis, downplaying the size of the changes proposed. “Looking at the order of magnitude of the content, you would say it’s not worth breaking up a government over this,” Marieke Blom Chief Economist and Global Head of Research at ING Group. “It’s symbolic, not essential from an economic perspective. The risk of another period of stagnation and/or regulatory uncertainty is more relevant at this time.” (Updates with result of parliament vote from the first paragraph.)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

headline: Greater Noida tourist dies after falling from paraglider at Himachal’s Bir-Billing
content: A 26-year-old tourist from Greater Noida died after falling from a tandem paraglider mid-air during a flight at the internationally renowned Bir-Billing paragliding site in Himachal Pradesh’s Kangra district on Tuesday evening. Police have registered a case against the pilot and launched an investigation into the incident. Police have identified the victim as Shubham Dobliyal (26). He was working with the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd (ONGC). Shubham, along with his sister Vanshika Dobliyal and three cousins, had reached Bir-Billing on Monday for tandem paragliding. They are residents of Supertech Eco Village 3, Greater Noida West, Noida Extension, NCR. The victim’s father, Kamal Singh, is serving in the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF). Police said all five had stayed in a hostel in Bir and reached Billing on Tuesday for paragliding at 4.10 pm. “Shubham was the first to take the tandem flight with pilot Vinay Kumar. Others followed him in their tandem flights,” they said. Police said that Pilot Vinay Kumar, along with other pilots and relatives of the victim, Shubham, had found the body in the dense forest first; a police team reached there subsequently. “We have not found the GoPro camera, which is usually given to record the in-air moments by the pilot, and the purse of victim Shubham Dobliyal was also not found at the spot,” they said. His body was retrieved from the Gharari Dhar area, near Bir-Billing, around 8.30 pm, nearly three and a half hours after the incident. The incident took place at the same time as a Russian paraglider, Aleksei Ivakhin, was being rescued yesterday evening. Ivakhin got stuck on a high-tension electrical wire in Mandi around 250 feet above the ground. Police said preliminary investigation suggests the passenger’s safety harness may have loosened or opened during the flight. However, the exact cause will be established only after a detailed investigation, they said. Police have seized the paraglider and the passenger seat for forensic examination. The body was handed over to the family after a postmortem examination at Baijnath Civil Hospital on Wednesday. Meanwhile, the victim’s sister, Vanshika, said that one of the cousins had noticed that Shubham was hanging with the paraglider when they were all in the air. She also alleged that the pilots did not show them the footage from their GoPro cameras, which recorded Shubham’s last moments, when he fell from the tandem paraglider. She told The Indian Express, “When Shubham fell from his paraglider, we were also in the air. I had a brief view of my brother… but one of my cousins had clearly seen Shubham while descending or falling from the paraglider. I am sure the last moments of my brother were also recorded in our GoPro cameras, but the pilots declined to share these videos with us.” Manish, one of the cousins, told The Indian Express, “All of us were paragliding. We learnt about the incident after landing when Shubham’s pilot informed us that Shubham had fallen at the landing site in Bir… Shubham’s pilot raised a hue and cry, gathered all his pilot and guide friends and launched a search operation. Some of us accompanied Vinay in his car to reach the forest where our brother had fallen.” Police said the missing GoPro camera is a hurdle to establishing the sequence of events. Police have registered a case of causing death due to negligence against pilot Vinay Kumar, a resident of Kotli village in Baijnath subdivision of Kangra, at Bir police station. The Kangra Superintendent of Police (SP), Kulbhushan Verma, said the exact cause of the incident was yet to be established. “The incident could have occurred either because the safety belt became loose or snapped during the flight, or because the pilot was performing manoeuvres. A detailed investigation is required to ascertain the exact cause.” The Deputy Commissioner (DC), Kangra, Hemraj Bairwa, said that the incident is being examined from all angles. SDM (Baijnath) Sankalp Gautam said, “It is a serious incident. We will take strict steps regarding the equipment and gliders of the firms offering tandem flights. It is the first incident this year wherein a passenger lost his life during tandem paragliding.” A paragliding instructor at Bir-Billing described the incident as a possible case of ‘free fall’, where either the passenger or the pilot falls from the paraglider before it reaches the landing site. The instructor said, “Such incidents could occur if safety harnesses were not properly fastened or if someone tampered with the safety belts during the flight. The possibility of the passenger having accidentally or deliberately opened the safety belt also needs to be examined.” Last month, solo paragliding flights at Bir-Billing in Kangra district were suspended following a series of hard landings, injuries and fatal accidents, including the death of a Bulgarian national, Maksim Valentinovich Gavrilichenko. Later, the suspension was lifted, subjecting it to mandatory compliance with the Himachal Pradesh Aero Sports Rules (HPASR), 2022, and the National Air Sports Guidelines (NASG), 2023. In July 2025, a 25-year-old tourist from Ahmedabad, Satish Rajesh Bhai, died, and a local pilot sustained injuries when their tandem paraglider crashed shortly after take-off from the Indrunag paragliding site near Dharamshala, which is at a considerable distance from the Bir-Billing paragliding site.

headline: He moved from Himachal Pradesh to Australia in 2008 to pursue higher education, worked part-time while st
content: An Indian-origin man from Himachal Pradesh has made history in Australia. Abhishek Awasthi, who hails from Lower Samkhetar in Mandi, has taken over as the Mayor of Greater Bendigo in Victoria, becoming the first person of Indian origin to hold the position in the city.As reported by The Tribune and various media, Awasthi, 43, took the oath of office on November 9, 2026, at a ceremony held at The Capital Theatre in Greater Bendigo. He has assumed the mayoral position for the 2026-27 term, which will last one year. His appointment is also a significant milestone for the Indian community in the region.From an international student in 2008 to Mayor in 2026Awasthi's journey to the mayor's office began when he moved to Australia in 2008 to pursue higher education. According to New India Abroad, he arrived in the country as an international student and eventually settled in Bendigo in 2010.As reported by The Tribune, he enrolled at La Trobe University, where he studied biotechnology and later earned a master's degree in bioinformatics. He also took up part-time work while completing his education. His move to Australia was followed by a career in public service. Over the years, he held several important positions in the Victorian state government. He became an Australian citizen in 2015 and now lives in Greater Bendigo with his wife, Anima, and daughter, Agni.According to The New Indian Express, Awasthi also became involved in community activities after settling in Bendigo. He participated in volunteering initiatives and programmes promoting multiculturalism. He also founded the Indian Association of Bendigo, which was formally established in 2021. The organisation works to bring Indian families across central Victoria together through cultural events, charitable activities and community support programmes.Entered local politics in 2024 and became Deputy MayorAwasthi's entry into electoral politics came in November 2024, when he won the councillor's election from Kennington Ward in Greater Bendigo. The city has nine wards.His election to the council was followed by another milestone. He became the first person of Indian origin to serve as Deputy Mayor of Greater Bendigo for the 2024-25 term, working alongside Andrea Metcalf, who was then the Mayor.Just two years after entering the city council, Awasthi was unanimously selected for the mayoral position for 2026-27. According to The Tribune, his parents and other relatives were present at the swearing-in ceremony to witness the occasion. His father, Surender Pal, is retired from the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB), while his mother, Champa Sharma, is a homemaker.What Abhishek Awasthi said after becoming MayorSpeaking to The Tribune’s Dipender Manta after his election, Awasthi expressed gratitude to his fellow councillors and the people of Greater Bendigo for trusting him with the responsibility."I am truly honoured and humbled to have been elected Mayor of the City of Greater Bendigo. Thanks to my fellow Councillors for their trust and confidence, and to our community for the opportunity to serve," he said.He also acknowledged the congratulatory messages he received from India, particularly from Himachal Pradesh and his hometown of Mandi. Awasthi also expressed his gratitude to his parents, relatives and everyone who had supported him throughout his journey.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. headline: Video: Paraglider trapped on high-tension wires in Himachal Pradesh; 146-metre crane used in rescue
content: A paraglider was rescued after getting entangled in high-tension power lines around 150 metres above the ground in Himachal Pradesh's Mandi district on Tuesday. The pilot remained suspended for nearly two-and-a-half hours before a rescue team brought him to safety using a 146-metre hydraulic crane.According to a report by The Times of India, the incident took place near Mehar village, around five kilometres from Mandi town. The paraglider got caught in the power lines along the Pathankot-Mandi highway during the afternoon.Other paragliders who witnessed the incident alerted the administration, following which the electricity supply was switched off, an official said.146-metre hydraulic crane deployed for rescue operationMandi Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) and police officials reached the spot, but bringing the pilot down from such a height posed a major challenge.The administration arranged a 146-metre hydraulic crane for the rescue operation. An SDRF personnel used the crane's basket to reach the stranded paraglider and bring him down safely.As a precautionary measure, people gathered at the site spread a tarpaulin and mattresses on the ground beneath the pilot in case he fell during the operation, TOI reported.Pathankot-Mandi highway closed to heavy vehiclesThe rescue operation also affected traffic along the Pathankot-Mandi highway. The road was closed to heavy vehicles while the crane was being assembled and the operation was underway.The pilot was subsequently brought down safely, bringing the challenging rescue operation to an end.

headline: Chhattisgarh Charts Roadmap to Harness India's Free Trade Agreements; C&I Minister Announces Chhattisgarh FTA Accelerator
content: The Department of Commerce, Government of India, in collaboration with the Department of Commerce & Industries, Government of Chhattisgarh, today organised a State-level workshop, “Leveraging FTAs – Outreach Programme”, in Raipur. The workshop aimed to build awareness among the State's industries and exporters of the opportunities opened up by India's recently signed Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), and to chart sector-wise strategies for deeper utilisation of these agreements. From the Government of Chhattisgarh: Shri Lakhan Lal Dewangan, Hon'ble Minister, Commerce & Industries; Shri Rajeev Agrawal, Chairman, CSIDC; Shri Rajat Kumar, Secretary, Department of Commerce & Industries; Shri Prabhat Malik, IAS, Director, Directorate of Industries. From the Government of India: Shri Manish Chadha, Joint Secretary, Department of Commerce; Dr. Praveen Kumar, Joint Director General of Foreign Trade, DGFT Regional Authority, Raipur; and Shri Girdhari Lal, DGFT Headquarters. Representatives of APEDA, TRIFED, Export Promotion Councils, industry associations and a large number of exporters also took part. The workshop included breakout sessions where exporters discussed about opportunities in Agriculture, Engineering, Handicrafts, Textiles and E commerce sectors of the State. Addressing the workshop, the Minister said Chhattisgarh's exports stood at about USD 2 billion last year, led by rice, steel, ferro-alloys and aluminium, alongside forest produce such as honey, lac, mahua and tamarind, and handicrafts such as Dhokra and Kosa. India has signed FTAs with the UAE, Australia, Oman, the United Kingdom and New Zealand, and the agreement with the European Union is expected to come into force in 2027. According to the Department of Commerce, 93 of the State's 95 export products now enjoy duty concessions in at least one partner market. The 5% duty on the State's steel and aluminium in Gulf countries is now zero, and the UK has eliminated duties of 18% on broken rice and 17% on honey. The State has notified the Chhattisgarh Export Promotion Policy 2026–30, which aims to double exports by 2030 and raise the State's share in India's exports from 0.5% to 1%. Chhattisgarh FTA Accelerator — a proposed initiative to hand-hold exporters from start to finish.

headline: Bhagni Nivedita Chhatri Niwash in Tripura
content: Access to safe and affordable accommodation is an important enabler of higher education, particularly for young women travelling from distant and rural areas. Bhagni Nivedita Chhatri Niwash, located at Krishnanagar, Agartala West, Tripura, is a hostel initiative to support girl students belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC) community as they pursue college and university education. The initiative highlights the role of targeted hostel infrastructure in advancing inclusive educational opportunities. On completion, the proposed 54-seat facility is expected to support OBC girl students travelling from distant areas and contribute to a more enabling environment for higher education. For students living far from educational institutions, finding suitable accommodation can present a practical challenge to continuing their studies. A dedicated hostel facility is meant to ease this difficulty and provide a more supportive environment in which students can focus on their academic goals. Bhagni Nivedita Chhatri Niwash has a planned capacity of 54 seats. The project information reports 20 current residents or beneficiaries. The facility is meant to provide accommodation to eligible OBC students and strengthen boarding arrangements. The project is being implemented by the Rural Development Department, Government of Tripura, on behalf of the OBC Welfare Department. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, is the funding and supporting agency. The facility reflects the importance of coordination between the Central and State Governments in supporting educational infrastructure.

headline: ICAR-NRC on Mithun, Nagaland Organises Khet Bachao Abhiyan and Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada 2026
content: ICAR–National Research Centre on Mithun, Medziphema, Nagaland, organised an awareness programme at Molovom village today as part of Khet Bachao Abhiyan and Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada 2026. During the programme, rural youth were sensitised about various entrepreneurship opportunities in agriculture and allied sectors. The discussions focused on livestock-based enterprises, value addition of locally available agricultural and livestock products, and the potential for starting small-scale rural businesses. The importance of skill development, effective utilisation of local resources and self-employment in generating additional income and livelihood opportunities was also highlighted. The programme aimed to encourage rural youth to explore entrepreneurship and contribute towards sustainable livelihood development in their communities. (Source: ICAR–National Research Centre on Mithun, Medziphema, Nagaland)

headline: Himachal Pradesh Government
content: Governor Kavinder Gupta today visited the 1,500 MW Nathpa Jhakri Hydro Power Station (NJHPS), operated by SJVN Limited, and reviewed its functioning, operational efficiency and contribution towards strengthening the nation's energy infrastructure. During the visit, Chief General Manager and Head of Project (NJHPS) Rajeev Kapoor briefed the Governor on the power generation capacity, operational achievements and technological advancements of the hydroelectric project. The Chief General Manager further apprised the Governor that several critical components and sophisticated equipment used in hydroelectric projects, which were earlier imported from foreign countries are now being manufactured indigenously in India, reflecting significant progress towards technological self-reliance. Expressing satisfaction over this development, the Governor said that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is witnessing remarkable progress in indigenous manufacturing through the Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat initiatives. He said that India's growing capabilities in manufacturing advanced equipment for major infrastructure projects demonstrate the country's determination to reduce import dependence and emerge as a technologically empowered, self-reliant nation. Describing hydropower as a vital pillar of India's clean energy future, the Governor said Himachal Pradesh possesses immense potential to strengthen national energy security while promoting sustainable development and economic growth.

headline: Himachal Pradesh Pollution Board Shuts 12 Stone Crushers in Kangra, Mandi
content: The Himachal Pradesh State Pollution Control Board (HPSPCB) has ordered the immediate closure of 12 stone crushers operating in the Kangra and Mandi districts of the state. The board has also directed electricity authorities to disconnect power supply to these units, marking an escalation in the crackdown against operations allegedly violating environmental regulations.Information was available with The Chenab Times indicating that the directive encompasses 10 stone crushers situated in Kangra district and two within Mandi district. Furthermore, the board has explicitly prohibited these units from utilizing diesel generators or any alternative power sources post-disconnection, effectively closing off any avenues for continued operation bypassing the closure order. Reports suggest that individual units in Dehra, Fatehpur, and Jaisinghpur, along with two units in Nurpur, have been issued cessation of operation notices. In Mandi district, the closure orders pertain to one crusher each in Karsog and Chachyot. The Executive Engineers of the concerned electricity divisions have been formally instructed to implement the power disconnections and ensure strict adherence to the closure orders.This decisive action has been initiated under the provisions of Section 33-A of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and Section 31-A of the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. These legislative clauses grant significant authority to pollution control bodies, empowering them to issue binding directives that include the closure of industrial facilities and the severance of essential utility supplies, such as electricity and water, in cases of non-compliance with environmental protection laws.Previously, the HPSPCB had taken similar punitive measures against 13 stone crushers located in Solan and Kangra districts. The recent orders targeting an additional 12 units underscore an expanding enforcement campaign, with a particular focus on Kangra, a region where the activities of stone crushers and associated mining operations have long been identified as significant environmental concerns demanding robust regulatory intervention.Rahul Sharma, the Regional Officer of the Pollution Control Board stationed in Dharamsala, stated that the units identified for closure had been served with two prior notices, offering 15 and then seven-day periods for compliance, but these notices were not adequately addressed within the stipulated timelines. Following the lack of response, the regional office forwarded its recommendation for power disconnection to the State Pollution Control Board for further action. Mr. Sharma elaborated that the non-compliant units had failed to renew their permanent registrations, and additionally, some of these facilities were found to be inadequately equipped with essential pollution control devices, thereby exacerbating their environmental impact and contravening established norms.The enforcement action by the Himachal Pradesh State Pollution Control Board targets multiple stone crushers for operating without the requisite permissions or in contravention of established environmental norms. The board's directives are aimed at curbing pollution and ensuring sustainable practices within the state's industrial sector, particularly in areas prone to mining and quarrying activities.The authorities are intensifying their scrutiny of industrial operations that impact air and water quality. The closure orders are a direct consequence of repeated violations and the failure of the implicated units to rectify their environmental compliance issues despite being given multiple opportunities to do so. The board's stance signals a firm commitment to upholding environmental standards and protecting the natural resources of Himachal Pradesh from detrimental industrial practices.The ongoing drive by the pollution control board reflects a broader national emphasis on environmental governance and the implementation of stringent regulations for industries. Stone crushers, by their nature, are significant sources of dust pollution and can impact water bodies if not managed responsibly. The actions taken in Kangra and Mandi are consistent with these broader environmental protection goals.The compliance with environmental regulations is crucial for the sustainable development of regions like Himachal Pradesh, which rely heavily on their natural beauty and ecological integrity for tourism and local livelihoods. The board's decision to disconnect power supply ensures that the closure is effective and prevents any ad-hoc resumption of activities, which could further damage the environment. The involvement of electricity authorities underscores the coordinated approach being adopted to enforce environmental laws.The affected stone crusher units have been operating in areas where mining and quarrying activities are prevalent. The environmental impact assessment and compliance monitoring of such units are critical to mitigate the negative consequences on local ecosystems and public health. The board's proactive measures are expected to bring about improved environmental conditions in the affected districts.The regulatory framework in India provides for stringent penalties and closure orders for industries that fail to adhere to environmental protection acts. The HPSPCB's actions align with these legal provisions, aiming to create a deterrent effect and promote responsible industrial behaviour across the state. The continuous monitoring and enforcement are key to ensuring the long-term effectiveness of these environmental measures.

headline: 'More you apply the brakes, more petrol is consumed': R Ashoka blames potholes for low mileage, says not due to ethanol-blended fuel
content: Bengaluru: Karnataka Leader of the Opposition R Ashoka on Thursday claimed that vehicle mileage had dropped not because of ethanol-blended petrol, but bad roads. The BJP leader said this at a news conference where he accused the Congress government of raising the issue of ethanol-blended fuel to divert public attention. "Congress and Chief Minister D K Shivakumar say that mileage had reduced. Mileage has reduced not because of petrol or diesel, but due to potholes on roads. Roads across Karnataka have developed potholes, resulting in low mileage," Ashoka said. .Karnataka not opposing ethanol, but against cheating people: Minister Rizwan Arshad .To substantiate his claim, Ashoka said the average speed of the state-run BMTC buses in Bengaluru had fallen from 18 km per hour to 11 km per hour. "This isn't because of traffic. It's due to potholes," he said. "The more you apply the brakes, the more petrol is consumed." Ashoka was reacting to the state government's findings last week that up to 31% ethanol was found blended in petrol based on samples that were tested. Consumer Affairs & Legal Metrology Minister Rizwan Arshad said the use of ethanol beyond the mandated 20% (E20) blending was impacting mileage and engine health. "Out of 63 samples, only 11 samples were shown. The test results of the remaining samples should also have been shown. Were the samples collected from Congress-owned petrol bunks? Which bunks? That has not been disclosed," Ashoka said. Ashoka said ethanol-blending was made into a controversy to "divert attention" away from "mistakes of the Congress government". No problem has been reported from Himachal Pradesh, Punjab or other states, Ashoka said. "Vehicle manufacturing companies have not complained that their engines are getting damaged, nor have people gone to court. Only Congress is complaining about this. Only Rizwan Arshad and Shivakumar are raising complaints," he said. According to to Ashoka, between 2014 and May 2026, ethanol blending had resulted in savings of Rs 1.90 lakh crore in foreign exchange for India. "Consumption of more than 310 lakh tonnes of crude oil has reduced, and about 930 lakh metric tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions have been reduced. Farmers have received more than Rs 1.60 lakh crore additional income," he said.

headline: Agnipath 2.0: Reform and rollback
content: The Agnipath scheme, the flagship recruitment programme for India’s armed forces, introduced in 2022 with much fanfare, is set for an unexpected overhaul: an optional two-year extension to the service period for 75% of the recruits due for exit after four years. Those who receive the extension would be offered permanent recruitment if they satisfy specific eligibility criteria and want to continue. It may help almost all willing and fit Agniveers to be absorbed into the forces. The Central government’s decision has come weeks before the first batch of Agniveers is scheduled to exit the forces. Since its inception, the scheme has been criticised on several grounds. But the reason for the overhaul appears more political than anything else. The government had defended the scheme against criticism, including from senior retired military officers, all these years. Of the seven states where Assembly elections are scheduled next year, at least four – Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, and Himachal Pradesh – contribute significantly to the forces. The scheme had caused discontent and triggered protests in these states. Now, the government may be trying to appease the job-seeking youth. .All Agniveers will be absorbed in regular cadre: Defence officials.One major criticism has been regarding the uncertainty faced by the recruits until the end of four years. This uncertainty might continue because 75% of the Agniveers will face another evaluation after two years. Those who are selected thus will be ranked below their one-time peers in some respects, creating two categories with unequal terms of service and prospects in a hierarchical system where seniority matters. This can create resentment. Doubts remain about whether the post-exit reservations in the central and state forces would continue. .Two major objectives of the scheme, as claimed by the government, were a drop in the average age of military personnel and a check on the ballooning salary and pension bills. The restructuring would go against these objectives. This means the government launched the scheme without fully thinking through its potential overall impact. The Narendra Modi government had claimed that the scheme was intended to strengthen the armed forces. By that logic, its redesign could end up counterproductive. The changes mean a virtual rollback of some of the scheme’s key elements, though its name and general design might remain. Also worrying is the lack of clarity over the future of the four-year scheme and the extended six-year programme. Policies in recruitment to the defence forces should not be experimental or tailored to political imperatives.

headline: Himachal Paragliding Tragedy: Tourist Falls To Death At Bir Billing; GoPro Camera Missing, Pilot Booked
content: A holiday in Himachal Pradesh’s popular paragliding destination, Bir Billing, ended in tragedy after a 26-year-old tourist from Greater Noida fell from a tandem paraglider during a flight on Tuesday evening. The tourist, identified as Shubham Dobliyal, died after plunging into a dense forest in Kangra district. Police have registered a case of causing death due to negligence against the pilot and launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident. According to a report in The Indian Express, Shubham, who worked with the Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC), had travelled to Bir-Billing with his sister Vanshika and three cousins. The family, residents of Supertech Eco Village 3 in Greater Noida West, had arrived on Monday and were staying at a hostel in Bir. What Happened During The Tandem Paragliding Flight? According to the police, the group reached Billing on Tuesday for paragliding at around 4:10 pm. Shubham was the first among them to take a tandem flight, accompanied by pilot Vinay Kumar. His sister and cousins followed in separate tandem flights. The incident reportedly occurred while Shubham was airborne. His body was eventually located in the Gharari Dhar area, near Bir-Billing, at around 8:30 pm, nearly three and a half hours after he fell. Police said pilot Vinay Kumar, along with other pilots and the victim’s relatives, initially found the body in the dense forest. A police team reached the location later and retrieved the body. One of Shubham’s cousins reportedly noticed him hanging from the paraglider while the group was still in the air. His sister also said she briefly saw her brother during the incident. Safety Harness Suspected; Paraglider Seized For Examination Preliminary police findings suggest that the passenger’s safety harness may have loosened or opened during the flight. However, investigators have not established the exact cause of the fall. Kangra Superintendent of Police Kulbhushan Verma said the incident could have occurred if the safety belt became loose or snapped, or if the pilot was performing manoeuvres. He said a detailed investigation would be necessary to determine what exactly happened. Police have seized the paraglider and the passenger seat for forensic examination. The absence of the GoPro camera, which is generally used by pilots to record tandem flights, has also emerged as an important aspect of the investigation. Police said the camera has not been recovered from the spot. The victim’s purse was also missing. Sister Alleges Pilots Refused To Share GoPro Footage Shubham’s sister, Vanshika, has alleged that the pilots did not show the family the footage recorded by their GoPro cameras, which she believes may have captured her brother’s final moments. Speaking to The Indian Express, she said she had a brief glimpse of Shubham after he fell, while one of her cousins had clearly seen him descending from the paraglider. She also claimed that the family was denied access to the recordings. One of the cousins said that the group learnt about the incident only after landing, when Shubham’s pilot informed them that he had fallen near the landing site in Bir. According to Manish, the pilot then alerted other pilots and guides and began searching for Shubham. Some family members accompanied him to the forest where the body was eventually found. Police have said that the missing GoPro camera could make it more difficult to establish the sequence of events leading to the fall. Pilot Booked; Family Receives Body After Postmortem Police have registered a case of causing death due to negligence against pilot Vinay Kumar, a resident of Kotli village in the Baijnath subdivision of Kangra district. The case has been filed at Bir police station. The Kangra Deputy Commissioner, Hemraj Bairwa, said the incident was being examined from all possible angles. Baijnath Sub-Divisional Magistrate Sankalp Gautam described it as a serious incident and said strict steps would be considered regarding the equipment and gliders used by firms offering tandem paragliding flights. Shubham’s body was taken to Baijnath Civil Hospital for a postmortem examination and handed over to his family on Wednesday. Instructor Points To Possible Free Fall A paragliding instructor at Bir Billing described the incident as a possible case of ‘free fall’, in which either the passenger or the pilot falls from the paraglider before it reaches the landing area. The instructor said such incidents could occur if safety harnesses were not fastened properly or if someone tampered with the safety belts during the flight. The possibility of a passenger accidentally or deliberately opening the belt would also need to be examined, the instructor added. These are possible explanations and have not been established as the cause of Shubham’s death. The police investigation and forensic examination are expected to shed more light on the incident. Bir-Billing Paragliding Safety Under Scrutiny After Earlier Accidents The latest death has renewed attention on safety arrangements at Bir-Billing, an internationally recognised paragliding destination in Kangra district. Last month, solo paragliding flights at the site were suspended following a series of hard landings, injuries and fatal accidents. These included the death of Bulgarian national Maksim Valentinovich Gavrilichenko. The suspension was subsequently lifted, subject to mandatory compliance with the Himachal Pradesh Aero Sports Rules, 2022, and the National Air Sports Guidelines, 2023. In July 2025, a 25-year-old tourist from Ahmedabad, Satish Rajesh Bhai, died after a tandem paraglider crashed shortly after taking off from the Indrunag paragliding site near Dharamshala. A local pilot was also injured. Indrunag is separate from the Bir-Billing paragliding site. Earlier, in April 2024, 56-year-old Ritu Chopra, a resident of Noida and wife of a former Indian Air Force officer, died after her paraglider crashed in the hills shortly after taking off from Bir Billing. With the latest fatality, the focus is once again on whether safety equipment, flight procedures and operator checks at Himachal Pradesh’s popular adventure tourism sites are being adequately enforced.

headline: DA hike pending arrears payment process: How money will be paid after states increased dearness allowance on Diwali
content: The Union Cabinet in October hiked dearness allowance (DA) and dearness relief (DR) by 3% for central government employees and pensioners, respectively. This raised the component from 60% to 63% of basic pay, effective from 1 July.Beneficiaries include more than 1 crore people, including around 50 lakh central government employees and some 65 lakh pensioners, including defence and railway personnel and retirees. This hike is the second this year under the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC) recommendations and comes after the government increased the allowance by 2% in April from 58% to 60%, effective from 1 January 2026.Besides the Finance Ministry's announcement on 28 October, state governments also hiked DA for employees and pensioners ahead of Diwali and Chhath Puja. This includes 2% hikes by the Chhattisgarh, Kerala and Madhya Pradesh governments each; 2.5% increase by the Karnataka government, 3% DA hikes each by the Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand governments; and 5% hike by the Himachal Pradesh government.DA hike: What are arrears payments? Is it mandatory?Arrears are payments due for the period between when salary revisions are applied and when they are actually paid. The amount is not automatically guaranteed and must be announced by the Centre or state governments. As a general guide, higher pay matrix levels and longer delays will likely result in larger salary and pension arrears for employees and pensioners, respectively.Here's a look at what we know about payment of the hiked DA and pending arrears:Punjab DA hike payment, arrearsEarlier this month, Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann announced a 3-percentage-point increase in DA for state government employees and pensioners, benefiting around 8 lakh beneficiaries. He added that the enhanced DA would be reflected in December salaries and pensions, PTI reported.With this announcement, the DA rate in Punjab has increased from 50% to 53%, effective from 1 November 2026, it added.How will the Arunachal Pradesh DA hike be paid?Arunachal Pradesh increased DA and DR for state government employees and pensioners by three percentage points, from 60% to 63%, effective from 1 July as a “Diwali bonanza”, Chief Minister Pema Khandu said.Besides state government employees and pensioners, the enhanced DA and DR will also benefit All India Services (AIS) officers serving under the state government as well as central government employees on deputation to Arunachal Pradesh and will be paid along with the salary and pension for the month of November, he added.The CM said that arrears for the four-month period from July to October will be paid in cash and credited directly to the respective salary accounts of serving employees and the pension accounts of pensioners and family pensioners.Uttarakhand DA payment to come in cashThe Uttarakhand government also approved a 3% DA for state employees, increasing the component to 63% of basic pay, with effect from 1 July 2026 under the 7th Central Pay Commission (CPC), Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami's Office said in a statement.The decision brings Uttarakhand state employees' DA on par with their central government counterparts, it added. The statement added that the differential amount, i.e. DA arrears, for the period from 1 July to 31 October 2026, will be paid in cash to eligible employees.Uttar Pradesh hikes DA by 3%Uttar Pradesh has increased dearness allowance by 3%, from 60% of basic pay to 63%, with effect from 1 July 2026, the state government said in an order issued last week. This decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the state and provide financial relief amid Diwali festivities, PTI reported.The increased DA for October will be paid along with regular salary for November 2026, according to the PTI report. Further, an ANI report added that arrears for the preceding four-month period between July and September 2026 will be deposited separately into employees' provident fund (PF) accounts.Disclaimer: This is for informational purposes only. Please visit the official government websites for the latest updates and notifications.

headline: Shimla Tourism Boosted by Cleaner Air After Diwali Pollution
content: Shimla, Himachal Pradesh is experiencing a significant influx of tourists who are seeking refuge from the hazardous air pollution levels that have enveloped neighbouring states, particularly Delhi, Punjab, and Haryana, in the aftermath of Diwali celebrations.Hill Station Offers Respite from Smog-Choked PlainsInformation was available with The Chenab Times that thousands of holidaymakers have been making their way to the popular hill station, with destinations like The Ridge, The Mall, Jakhu, Kufri, and Naldehra witnessing large crowds. While Shimla also registered a rise in air pollution post-Diwali, its Air Quality Index (AQI) remained at a comparatively satisfactory level of 66, a notable improvement from the dangerous conditions reported in the plains.The air quality in the National Capital Region (NCR) had soared to approximately 450, prompting many families to seek cleaner air in the mountains. Tourists from Delhi, Punjab, and Haryana are prominent among the visitors, but the hill station is also attracting travellers from as far as West Bengal, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, and Gujarat.Kulbhushan Gupta, a tourist from Delhi, shared his experience, stating that the AQI in the national capital was alarmingly high, making their trip to Shimla a necessary escape. "The weather here is very pleasant and the AQI is around 66, which is much better than Delhi. The air is fresher and has provided us considerable relief from pollution," Gupta said. Similarly, Apoorva Shekhawat, who travelled to Shimla with friends from Kotputli in Rajasthan, described the move to the hills as a welcome relief from the pervasive pollution across the NCR.The surge in tourist arrivals has provided a much-needed boost to Shimla's hospitality sector. Hoteliers have reported average occupancy rates ranging between 40 and 50 per cent, even on weekdays, indicating a positive trend in business. Tourism stakeholders are optimistic that this influx will continue and potentially increase in the coming days, further invigorating the local economy.The phenomenon highlights a growing trend where environmental conditions in densely populated plains are driving seasonal tourism to cooler, less polluted mountain regions. This shift underscores the importance of maintaining environmental quality in tourist destinations, as well as the increasing awareness among the public regarding the health impacts of air pollution. The contrast in air quality serves as a stark reminder of the environmental challenges faced by major urban centres in India during festive periods.Local authorities and tourism operators are working to accommodate the increased visitor numbers, ensuring that the infrastructure and services can meet the demand. The extended Diwali holiday period, combined with the appeal of Shimla's natural beauty and comparatively cleaner air, has created a perfect storm for a tourism rebound in the region. The positive economic impact on hotels, restaurants, and local businesses is anticipated to be substantial, providing a welcome stimulus after periods of reduced activity.The demand for hill stations as havens from urban pollution is expected to remain strong, potentially influencing travel patterns and tourism strategies in the future. As more people become conscious of air quality, destinations like Shimla are likely to see sustained interest, especially during periods when pollution levels are critical elsewhere. This trend also presents an opportunity for sustainable tourism development in Himachal Pradesh, focusing on preserving the environmental integrity that attracts visitors.The influx of tourists seeking cleaner air is a direct consequence of the severe air pollution incidents that have become a recurring issue in several parts of North India, particularly following Diwali. The astronomical rise in particulate matter and other pollutants creates not only discomfort but also poses significant health risks, compelling individuals and families to seek alternative destinations for recreation and respite. Shimla, with its well-established tourism infrastructure and reputation for scenic beauty, naturally becomes a preferred choice for such travellers.The hospitality sector in Shimla has responded to the increased demand by ensuring services are operational and that visitors have a comfortable stay. The positive reception from tourists regarding the air quality and the overall pleasant weather is a testament to the enduring appeal of the hill station. This surge in visitors is expected to contribute significantly to the local economy, supporting livelihoods and businesses dependent on tourism.The ongoing situation further emphasizes the need for effective pollution control measures in the plains, especially during the festive season. While Shimla benefits from this environmental disparity, the long-term sustainability of such tourism relies on the health of its own environment. The current scenario, however, provides a temporary but significant economic uplift for the region as it attracts those looking for a breath of fresh air.

headline: Himcahal primary teachers association postpone November 15 Dharamshala rally after talks with Education Director
content: Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 12 (ANI): The Himachal Pradesh Primary Teachers Association has postponed its proposed protest demonstration and mass rally scheduled to be held in Dharamshala on November 15 following a positive outcome of talks with the Director of Elementary Education, officials said on November 11.However, the association has decided to continue its chain hunger strike in Shimla, which entered its 109th day on Wednesday, until its demands receive formal approval from the state government and are implemented on the ground.The meeting was held with Director of Elementary Education Ashish Kohli following directions from Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. Association representatives said an agreement had been reached on most of their demands, and a further meeting with the Chief Minister would be held shortly to formally approve the agreed proposals.Speaking to ANI after the meeting, Ramesh Sharma, president of the Himachal Pradesh Primary Teachers Association, said the positive discussions had prompted the organisation to defer its proposed Dharamshala agitation, although it would not call off the ongoing hunger strike until concrete decisions were taken."Following directions from the Chief Minister, we held a meeting with the Director of Elementary Education today. An agreement has been reached on most of our demands. A further meeting with the Chief Minister will be held to formally approve these decisions. Until then, our chain hunger strike will continue. In view of the positive discussions, we have postponed the proposed November 15 protest and rally in Dharamshala," said Sharma. The teachers have been protesting against the revised cluster system, particularly issues concerning primary education and the interests of primary teachers. Their 25-point charter of demands also includes filling vacant posts of primary and nursery teachers, recruitment of caretakers, restoration of opportunities for Junior Basic Training (JBT) teachers, and addressing concerns related to the functioning of primary schools.The association has also raised concerns over the discontinuation of play activities for young children in schools and the appointment of Centre Head Teachers in CBSE schools.Sharma said the association would not declare victory merely on the basis of assurances, as previous discussions had also resulted in commitments that were never implemented on the ground."We do not want to claim victory at this stage because unless the decisions are notified and implemented on the ground, the association cannot make any such announcement. We have faith in the Chief Minister's assurances and hope that the Education Department will honour the commitments made during today's meeting. We have been told that the formal process with the Chief Minister will be completed within a week or ten days. Until then, our agitation will continue," added Sharma. The association said its agitation began with a 15-day foot march undertaken by primary teachers from different parts of the state during the summer vacation, followed by a massive protest in Shimla and the ongoing chain hunger strike.Sharma maintained that the association had ensured that its agitation did not disrupt academic activities. He said the foot march was organised during summer vacations, while other demonstrations were held on holidays and Sundays. During the chain hunger strike, only four teachers participated on a rotational basis each day, representing the association's state, district, women's wing and 143 block-level units."We have ensured that the education of children is not affected by our movement. Our foot march was held during the summer vacations, and the demonstrations were organised on Sundays. During the chain hunger strike, teachers participated on a rotational basis, with representatives from our different organisational units taking part for one day. We are happy that the academic activities of children have not suffered, and we will continue to ensure that their studies remain unaffected," said Sharma. He also acknowledged the support extended to the movement by mid-day meal workers, multi-task workers, unemployed youth, School Management Committee members, panchayat representatives, retired teachers and other sections of society.The association said teachers had remained united throughout the agitation, including during major festivals such as Dussehra, Diwali and Bhai Dooj, reflecting the seriousness of their concerns over primary education and the future of the teaching community.The teachers have maintained that their movement is aimed not only at protecting their service-related interests but also at strengthening the primary education system in Himachal Pradesh.With the Dharamshala rally postponed, the association is now awaiting the proposed meeting with the Chief Minister and formal government decisions on its 25-point charter of demands. The chain hunger strike, meanwhile, will continue until the assurances translate into concrete action. (ANI)

headline: Himachal CM announces Rs 18 crore for strengthening dental infrastructure
content: Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 12 (ANI): Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu today held an interaction with dental doctors to discuss measures to strengthen and improve dental services in the state.During the interaction, the Chief Minister reiterated the state government's commitment to offer world-class, accessible and technologically advanced health care services to the people of the State.Sukhu stated that the state government had already released Rs. 5.10 crore in the first phase for strengthening dental health care services and announced an additional allocation of Rs. 18 crore for further strengthening dental infrastructure in the state. He said that the Government would provide advanced equipment to Rajiv Gandhi Government Dental College, Shimla, including high-end dental chairs, CBCT machines, intraoral scanners and operation theatre tables.He said that these advanced facilities would not only enhance the working efficiency of the dental professionals but also ensure better diagnosis and treatment of patients. He assured that adequate para-medical staff would be deployed to support dental doctors in delivering efficient health care services. He also emphasised the need to strengthen dental radiology services through the provision of modern equipment.The Chief Minister said that a state-of-the-art Dental College and Centre of Excellence was being established at Hamirpur with an estimated cost of Rs. 600 crore. He said that the state government is also exploring the possibilities of constructing a new campus for the dental college at Chamiyana. He said that senior residency policy would also be implemented in dental colleges to strengthen academic and clinical services.He further said that lecturers would be promoted to the post of Assistant Professor, thereby creating better career progression for dental faculty. He added that an anesthesiologist would be made available at the dental college Shimla and dental chairs would also be installed in Trauma Centres to facilitate timely dental treatment in emergency situations.Sukhu assured the deployment of multi-task workers with the dental doctors to assist them in their functioning in PHCs, CHCs and District Hospitals. He said that several important issues had emerged during the interaction and the Government was committed to addressing their concerns. He further said that the Government was considering granting NPA to the dental doctors. He also asked the dental doctors to make optimum use of modern technology for transforming the quality of dental health care in the state.Health and Family Welfare Minister Dr (Col) Dhani Ram Shandil, while appreciating the Chief Minister's initiatives, said that the Chief Minister had consistently accorded priority to strengthening health care infrastructure across the state. He said that technological upgradation would be undertaken not only in medical colleges but also in dental colleges to ensure better health care delivery. He thanked the Chief Minister for providing an additional Rs. 18 crore for improving dental services in the state.Secretary Health Ashish Singhmar, Director Health Services Dr Gopal Beri and other senior officers were also present on the occasion. (ANI)
